summary: Arizona State University's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program offers 30 fully funded master's scholarships in technology and innovation to young Africans starting in 2027. The application window for this cohort closed on Sunday 27 September 2026 at 23:59 GMT.
meta_title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars at ASU: funding and deadlines
meta_description: Arizona State University's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program: fully funded master's in technology and innovation for young Africans. How to apply.
covers: Full tuition and fees for an on-campus master's degree at ASU.
On-campus housing and books, plus visa, airfare and medical expenses.
Leadership development, academic advising and a two-month internship between the first and second years.
eligibility: Young Africans aged 18 to 33 when they apply.
A bachelor's degree or equivalent, conferred by July 2027; a Higher National Diploma alone does not qualify.
No master's degree started or completed anywhere.
Women, refugees and displaced people, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Choose one of the nine eligible programmes: MS Global Technology and Development, Information Technology, Human Systems Engineering (Intelligent Systems), Computer Science, Data Science, Analytics and Engineering, Robotics and Autonomous Systems, Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering, Clean Energy Systems, or Modern Energy Production and Sustainable Use.
The 2027-28 cohort's application window closed on Sunday 27 September 2026 at 23:59 GMT; check the official page for details of the next call.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed, then guided to apply for ASU admission with an application fee waiver.
Scholarship decisions are made in early 2027.
watch_out: Apply for the scholarship first. Do not pay ASU's application fee or an English test yourself; waivers come if you reach the interview stage, and earlier payments are not refunded.
You can choose only one programme, and you cannot change it after you submit.
Scholars are strongly encouraged to return home after graduating; it is central to the Foundation's mission.
costs: Tuition, fees, on-campus housing and books
Waived, but only once you reach the interview stage
Duolingo English Test, if you need one
Waived by the programme after you advance; do not pay for a test in advance
documents: The scholarship application form, with answers in English
Your essay responses and a résumé/CV
One signed recommendation letter as a PDF, written within the past three years; it can be non-academic
An unofficial or official transcript; French is accepted at this stage
Optional: proof of English. It is not required to apply
Every file as a PDF, with your name in the file name

faq.q: Can I still apply for the 2027-28 cohort?
faq.a: No. The application window for this cohort closed on Sunday 27 September 2026 at 23:59 GMT. Check the official programme page for news of the next call.

faq.q: Can my documents be in French?
faq.a: Yes. Write the online form in English, but your letter, CV and transcripts can be in French; the team has French-speaking staff. An official translation is needed only if you become a finalist.

faq.q: Can I work in the US or stay after graduating?
faq.a: You may work within F-1 student visa rules and ASU policies. After graduation the scholarship strongly encourages you to return home.
